_comment: Adjudicated removals — compounds that are not physiologically active substances anyone doses, and rows that carry no pharmacology at all (a detail screen whose only content is a banner saying there is no content). Applied by SQLiteBuilder.drop_removed_substances(), which deliberately OUTRANKS the curated layer: a curated file is usually what kept an empty row alive, so removing a name here means deleting its data/curated/substances/*.json too (the build warns if one is left behind). Matching is on canonical_name only, never aliases — junk rows routinely share an alias with a legitimate one. Verdicts: not_a_substance (reagent, diagnostic analyte, cosmetic-cream ingredient, chemical-class name, protonated-cation record, vendor SKU), no_relevant_activity (real molecule, no activity a dose tracker can model), no_content (real compound, zero pharmacology in the catalog), catalog_noise (paper/patent/trial-only, never in human circulation), duplicate (supersededBy names the survivor). contentRowsAtRemoval records how many fact rows the entry held when it was cut, so a reviewer can see nothing substantial was thrown away. Each entry carries its own evidence; nothing here was removed on a hunch.
